heading: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - WAITING AREA - DAY

units.text: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - WAITING AREA - DAY
Rain taps the high windows.
A fluorescent tube flickers over a row of orange plastic chairs.
The radiator ticks.
Somewhere a vending machine hums to itself.
Marcus Doyle, 30s, sits with his hands between his knees, a manila folder resting in his lap.
Across from him, Rowan Pierce, 20s, slouches in a chair, scrolling a cracked phone.
Rowan uses they/them pronouns and wears a battered denim jacket.
You're early.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: Habit. They count it against you if you're late.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: Everybody counts everything against you.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: The fluorescent tube buzzes, dims, steadies.
Wind pushes at the glass.
ANGLE ON the reception desk.
MRS. HALE, 60s, sits behind a wall of plexiglass, glasses low on her nose, stamping a stack of forms.
Doyle. Marcus. You're up in five. Pierce, you're after.
units.name: MRS. HALE

units.text: Thank you, ma'am.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: Ma'am. Jesus.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: The intercom on the wall CRACKLES.
A man's voice, thin and wrong.
Hale, send Doyle back now. Skip the line.
units.name: OFFICER VANCE

units.text: Officer Vance, he's not on until--
units.name: MRS. HALE

units.text: Now.
units.name: OFFICER VANCE

units.text: Mrs. Hale hesitates.
The tube overhead goes out entirely.
The room is grey and green with rain-light.
That's not his voice.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: What do you mean it's not his voice?
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: Vance has a limp in his voice. I mean he whistles on his s's. That was somebody doing him.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: CLOSE ON the intercom's red light.
It blinks.
Once.
Twice.
Doyle. Don't make me ask again.
units.name: OFFICER VANCE

units.text: Don't go.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: I have to. If I don't show, it's a violation.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: It's a trap.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: It's always a trap.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: WE SEE the hallway door behind Mrs. Hale.
It is open an inch.
Beyond it, only darkness.
Don't go in there, honey.
units.name: MRS. HALE
paren: very quietly, not looking at either of them

units.text: INSERT - the desk calendar.
Today's date is circled in red.
Under it, in handwriting: "THEY COME BACK."
Who wrote that?
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: I did. Thirty years ago.
units.name: MRS. HALE

units.text: The radiator stops ticking.
The rain stops.
Even the vending machine goes silent.
Marcus. Look at the window.
units.name: ROWAN

units.text: BACK TO SCENE.
Reflected in the dark glass: the three of them, and a fourth shape standing in the open hallway door behind them, tall and still.
Doyle. Pierce. Hale. Come in. Come in. Come in.
units.name: OFFICER VANCE
paren: from the intercom, from the hallway, from everywhere
